Implementation Plan

Planning for the `{{NAME}}` placeholder secret leak in `scripts/render_prompt.sh` (refs #3576).

Planning ref: branch `ai/issue-9341` at commit `8b41834a7f1a2a4d501e4a731493a9f9b7994df1`. Integration branch mismatch: false. `scripts/render_prompt.sh` is identical on this branch and on `isolated-base`.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/render_prompt.sh`
- `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`
- `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`
- `tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py`
- `changelog.d/render-prompt-env-placeholder-secret-leak.md` (new)

## Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py::test_render_prompt_sh_does_not_forward_env_into_untrusted_body red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py::test_render_prompt_sh_refuses_secret_like_env_placeholders_in_trusted_template red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py::test_review_body_renders_run_with_secrets_unset red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py::test_render_prompt_sh_renders_implement_contract_defaults_and_env_values
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: the change is limited to helper scripts and tests, and the PR's CI test run fully covers it

## What the code does now
- `scripts/render_prompt.sh`, lines 304-309 on this ref: `collect_prompt_placeholders` lists every `{{NAME}}` in the body. For each name that is set in the environment, the loop calls `append_render_var "${placeholder_name}" "${!placeholder_name}"`. There is no allowlist and no check on the name.
- There are three callers that render untrusted bodies (raw PR diff, comments, findings). Each one sets `RENDER_PROMPT_INPUT_ALREADY_ASSEMBLED=1 RENDER_PROMPT_SKIP_SYNTAX_VALIDATION=1`:
  - `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:3059` (reviewer body)
  - `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:3213` (model-family overlay render)
  - `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1946` (editor body)
  No other script or workflow sets either variable.
- These bodies only need four scaffolding placeholders: `WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION`, `SEMBLE_PREFETCH`, `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS` and `MODEL_FAMILY_OVERLAY`. All four are already passed explicitly by `append_render_var` at lines 299-302, before the loop runs. So the loop adds nothing to these bodies except values whose names an attacker controls.
- `render_prompt.py` reads only fixed environment names (`collect_legacy_env_values`, the overlay and flag variables). It never looks up a name taken from the body, so it does not change.
- No placeholder in `prompts/`, `scripts/`, `.github/` or `workflow-templates/` contains TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PAT or PASSWORD. The only hit is a `{{KEY}}` inside a comment in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:2546`, which uses a different renderer.

## Functions or modules to implement
1. `scripts/render_prompt.sh`: add a function `render_prompt_env_name_is_secret_like`. It upper-cases the name (`${1^^}`) and returns 0 when the name matches `*TOKEN*|*KEY*|*SECRET*|*PAT*|*PASSWORD*|*PASSWD*|*CREDENTIAL*`. The first five patterns come from the finding; `PASSWD` and `CREDENTIAL` are a small, conservative addition.
2. `scripts/render_prompt.sh`: compute `RENDER_PROMPT_UNTRUSTED_BODY=true` when either `RENDER_PROMPT_INPUT_ALREADY_ASSEMBLED` or `RENDER_PROMPT_SKIP_SYNTAX_VALIDATION` is truthy. Use the same `1|true|yes|on|y` case patterns the script already uses. Base this only on what the caller set in the environment, never on `INPUT_ALREADY_ASSEMBLED_FLAG_ADDED`: the trusted `PROMPT_PRELUDE_REFACTOR_ENABLED` assembly path sets that flag internally.
3. `scripts/render_prompt.sh`: change the placeholder loop.
   - When `RENDER_PROMPT_UNTRUSTED_BODY=true`, skip the loop entirely. Only the four explicit `append_render_var` values are passed.
   - Otherwise (trusted templates), skip any name for which `render_prompt_env_name_is_secret_like` returns true. Print one stderr line per skipped name, of the form `WARNING: render_prompt.sh: refusing to forward secret-like environment placeholder <NAME>`. The line gives the name only, never the value. It deliberately has no bracketed prefix, so no new stable log prefix needs registering.
   - Add a comment that cites this finding.
4. `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` (lines 3059 and 3213) and `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh` (line 1946): put `env -u GH_TOKEN -u GH_PAT -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY -u TG_BOT_SECRET` in front of the existing `VAR=… bash …/render_prompt.sh` command. This follows the existing pattern in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3442` and `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh:50`.
   - `env` treats the `NAME=VALUE` words after its options as assignments, so the existing assignments keep working.
   - The substring that `tests/test_review_semble_contract.py:514` asserts (`SERENA_TOOL_HINTS="${EDITOR_SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}" bash "${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR}/render_prompt.sh" "${EDITOR_PROMPT_BODY_FILE}"`) stays byte-identical, because the prefix is added before it.
   - Keep the existing `( cd …; … ) > file` subshell, and the `if ! (…)` wrapper at line 3213.
5. Add a changelog fragment marked `<!-- changelog: security -->` that describes the fix and says `Refs #3576`.

## Data structures affected
- None persisted. Only the `RENDER_ARGS` / `RENDER_VARS_SEEN` arrays inside `scripts/render_prompt.sh` hold fewer entries.

## API or interface changes
- There are no new environment variables to set, CLI flags or log prefixes. `RENDER_PROMPT_UNTRUSTED_BODY` is computed inside the script and is never read from the environment.
- Behaviour change on the untrusted path: a `{{NAME}}` in an embedded diff or comment now stays literal, even when an environment variable called NAME exists. The four scaffolding names still render.
- Behaviour change on the trusted path: a placeholder with a secret-like name is no longer filled from the environment. It stays literal, and contract modes still report `missing_required` if the contract requires it.

Data flow:
1. The caller writes a body that contains untrusted text.
2. The caller runs `env -u <secrets> … render_prompt.sh` with both flags set.
3. `render_prompt.sh` sets `RENDER_PROMPT_UNTRUSTED_BODY=true`, passes the four explicit values and skips the environment loop.
4. `render_prompt.py` replaces only the values it was given, and the output body goes to the model.

Failure modes:
- A trusted template adds a placeholder whose name contains a denied substring, such as `FILE_PATH`, which contains `PAT`. Symptom: the stderr warning, plus a literal `{{FILE_PATH}}` in the output, or `missing_required` for a contract mode. Fix: pass it with an explicit `--var` route, or rename the placeholder.
- A newer reviewer prompt starts needing a forwarded environment value. Symptom: a literal placeholder in the reviewer prompt. Fix: add it as an explicit `append_render_var` in `render_prompt.sh`.

## Decisions
### D1 — Skip environment forwarding on untrusted bodies; keep it on trusted templates behind a name denylist
- Chosen: skip the loop when either untrusted flag is set. Keep the loop for trusted templates, but refuse names that look like secrets.
- Alternatives considered: (a) a global fixed allowlist of names; (b) forward only names in the mode contract's `required_vars`/`optional_vars`, which would need contract parsing in bash or a new `render_prompt.py` flag; (c) denylist only.
- Why: many trusted templates rely on environment values that are not in any short allowlist, so (a) and (b) risk silent regressions in clarify, plan and implement prompts. The untrusted bodies need none of the forwarded values, so skipping the loop there removes the attack completely. The denylist covers trusted templates as well.

### D2 — Unset secrets at the three call sites as defense in depth
- Chosen: put `env -u GH_TOKEN -u GH_PAT -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY -u TG_BOT_SECRET` before each untrusted render command in the scripts.
- Alternatives considered: unset them in the `review_autofix.yml` step `env:`; unset them inside `render_prompt.sh`.
- Why: the step needs `GH_TOKEN` for other work, and the workflow file is close to its size limit. The fix in `render_prompt.sh` already covers the general case; the per-call `env -u` is the second, independent layer the finding asks for, and it reuses an existing repository pattern.

### D3 — Log refused names as a plain WARNING
- Chosen: a single `WARNING: render_prompt.sh: …` stderr line that gives the name only.
- Alternatives considered: refuse silently; add a new stable log prefix.
- Why: a silent refusal would hide template mistakes. A new prefix would need registering through an agents.d fragment, which is more than this fix needs. The value is never printed.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the untrusted content is the PR diff, comments, check-run text and reviewer findings, which go to third-party model providers. Process environment secrets must never reach that content.
- Abuse case 1: a PR author puts `{{GH_TOKEN}}` or `{{OPENROUTER_API_KEY}}` in a changed file or a comment. After the fix it stays literal, because the loop is skipped. Even without that, the value is unset at the call site and the name is denied.
- Abuse case 2: a lowercase or mixed-case variant such as `{{gh_token}}`. Shell variable names are case-sensitive, so this only matches a lowercase variable, and the upper-casing in the denylist catches it on the trusted path.
- Abuse case 3: a body that sets only one of the two flags. Either flag on its own is enough to skip the loop.
- Abuse case 4: an attacker sets the flags themselves. That is not possible: the flags come from the caller's command line, not from the body.
- No new endpoint or authorization surface. No money handling. The stderr warning carries the name only, never the value.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- Conflict with the issue text: the finding cites `scripts/render_prompt.sh:314` and `:325-326`. On this ref the file has 316 lines, and the loop is at lines 304-309.
